text:
The text contrasts two perspectives on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, as evidenced by the boys' descent into savagery when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy suggests that society is the corrupting force, implying that humanity’s natural state is inherently good and free. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the origin of human behavior and morality, but they differ in their conclusions: Golding locates the source of evil within the individual, while Rousseau locates it in external societal structures.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
